subject: Discovery recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to confirm next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points you shared
- Streaming UX is intermittently slow: interactive chat shows partial token delays and whole-response stalls under peak.
- Observed p95 latency spikes up to ~2s for streaming responses (baseline ~500ms).
- Concurrency pressure from product: target sustained concurrency of ~150–200 active sessions during peak (30–45 RPS of streaming requests).
- Cache warm-up / cold-starts and retry storms when ModelCo rate limits cause request pile-ups.

Current stack (high level)
- Frontend: React chat with streaming SSE.
- Backend: Node-based API that proxies to ModelCo (hosted) on AWS g4dn instances. No in-house batching; occasional Redis prefix cache.

Success criteria you mentioned
- p95 streaming latency <= 350ms for single-turn chat interactions (goal: <=300ms if possible).
- Maintain 150 active concurrent streaming sessions for 30+ minutes without p95 degradation.
- Error rate < 5% and graceful degraded UX (partial tokens) when capacity strained.

Proposed next steps
1) You to share canonical load profile and a sample of prompts (we can use for replays) — we agreed on a CSV of 1-minute-resolution traffic (tokens per request, avg prompt length).
2) Redwood to run a 2-week PoC with Dedicated capacity + streaming-enabled runtime. We'll provide a short SOW and success metrics.
3) SE bench: Aditya will validate p95 latency and concurrency targets with a synthetic replay on a mirror environment.
4) Follow-up call next week to confirm timeline and any contract/PO items.

Attachments (sent): finly-load-profile.csv (placeholder for when you drop it here), redwood-poc-sow.pdf (draft).

Recording and notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example/meeting-recording
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-9742

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Marissa — thanks for the thorough summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Model provider: we currently proxy to ModelCo (managed) and run it on g4dn; their autoscaling sometimes lags which causes the 2s spikes.
- Typical prompt sizes: average 120 tokens, tail at ~600 tokens for longer context.
- Expected sustained peak: 150 concurrent active chat sessions, with bursts to ~220 during promotional events.

Success criteria (internal) — we're comfortable with your listed targets but can accept p95 <= 400ms as an initial SLA for pilot if Redwood can consistently hit <=350ms during the bench.

I've attached a simple architecture diagram and a sample traffic CSV — attaching finly-arch-diagram.png and the load CSV in this thread (I'll upload to Drive and share shortly).

Next steps from Finly
- I'll drop the canonical load_profile.csv in the shared Drive (today).
- Priya (cc) will coordinate procurement/NDAs if we move to pilot.
- Let's tentatively schedule the bench for the week of Sep 7.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Hi Alex — quick technical follow-ups so we size the bench correctly:

1) Streaming settings: are you using token-level streaming (SSE) with small token flushes (1–2 token chunks) or larger buffer flushes? This affects buffer/latency tradeoffs.
2) Average and 95th percentile prompt length in tokens (you gave average ~120 — can you share p95 token count)?
3) Typical response length (tokens) and whether users often request follow-up/edits causing multi-turn sessions.
4) Do you have a preferred retry/backoff policy we should mirror in the replay? Excessive client retries are a big cause of pile-ups.

Proposed bench plan
- Mirror: replay 30m of traffic scaled to 1h at target concurrency to profile p95 and tail behavior.
- Variants: test with Redwood Dedicated (quantized model variant) and Hosted fallback to emulate degradation.
- Metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 for streaming chunk latency, end-to-end p95 for full responses, error rate, and token throughput.

If you can drop the load_profile.csv and a short sample of prompts today we'll start baseline profiling and confirm exact bench schedule.

Cheers,
